title: Treat the canvas as an observed atlas, not a simultaneous page
userProblem: Byron needs to inspect content across time without introducing fictitious page states.
proposal: Keep immutable source-frame provenance for each owned image patch. Separate surface geometry, visual states and chronological visits. Leave unseen areas unknown; label composites as multi-time observations. Never fill gaps or carry old offscreen pixels into a new state as current evidence.

benefit: Preserves the distinctive scroll reconstruction while making its uncertainty inspectable.
cost: Patch ownership and visit bookkeeping; visible gaps can make the result less seamless.

confidence.level: high for evidence rules; unproven for useful automatic reconstruction

title: Start with guarded translation and a keyframe comparator
userProblem: A personal developer needs one small reconstruction engine rather than an ensemble.
proposal: Use optional Python analysis with OpenCV phase correlation, regional agreement and full-resolution integer-translation verification. Select one viewport per proof clip. Stitch only adequately textured, overlapping, stable-scale content. Split/refuse nested motion, scale/layout changes and ambiguous repetition. Keep change-selected cards as both fallback and comparator.

title: Run reconstruction offline and cache it independently of review edits
userProblem: Analysis must not destabilize recording or rerun whenever a note changes.
proposal: Propose scripts/analyze_canvas.py as an explicit offline operation. Store canvas.json and canvas/ as derived output keyed by video digest, analysis version and parameters. Let process_session.py optionally embed a valid sidecar; do not make capture or every reprocess invocation run reconstruction. Preserve old review behavior when output is absent, invalid or stale.

benefit: Keeps canonical recordings untouched and allows deterministic experiments on disposable copies.

title: Prove the spatial interaction in the portable HTML viewer
userProblem: Byron needs a navigable canvas before investing in native rendering infrastructure.
proposal: Add a proposed Canvas view alongside the existing video/timeline. Render bounded images in a transformed DOM layer with chronological visit buttons and a shared video.currentTime. Put states rightward and page geometry downward. Keep keyboard-accessible temporal navigation and an overview. Integrate SwiftUI only after the proof wins.

title: Preserve changes, motion and return visits instead of deduplicating time
userProblem: An attractive mosaic must not erase edits, animations or the later explanation of repeated content.
proposal: Create a new rightward state on detected content/layout change. Represent motion as a poster with a playable source interval and expandable temporal cards. Keep a chronological node for every revisit; use URL only to shortlist identity candidates. A confirmed return must name the matched region and its earlier/later witness frames.

title: Use actual video PTS and keep transcript association temporal
userProblem: Canvas clicks and narration must lead back to a defined observation, despite mixed clocks and coordinate systems.
proposal: Use decoded presentation timestamps, source-video pixel coordinates and explicit transforms. Do not treat mark-request time as still-exposure time, bridge receipt time as browser event time, or cached mark JPEGs as frame-exact evidence. Start with sentence-to-visit overlap labeled spoken-during; retain raw token references for later refinement without inventing semantic region grounding.

title: Bound image memory and make composite capture carry provenance
userProblem: Tall pages and hour-long sessions must remain inspectable without allocating a giant bitmap.
proposal: Use at-most-1024-square lossless evidence tiles/patches, overview thumbnails and explicit LRU eviction. Export a selected surface region offline as a bounded PNG plus provenance JSON; larger selections become numbered parts. Label multi-time images and keep Product Grid export separate until the artifact semantics are explicit.

title: Add browser measurements only after a specific visual failure earns them
userProblem: Browser assistance may improve viewport/scroll identity, but the recording must also work for supplied video-only lectures.
proposal: Keep current page events as coarse labels and candidates. If ROI/scroll ambiguity blocks otherwise useful clips, add sampled top-level and identified nested scroll geometry, zoom/visual-viewport data, document identity and a calibrated browser-to-host clock. Continue validating with video pixels. Defer rrweb and never fill observed surfaces from MHTML/DOM content.

title: Use four decisive gates before broad implementation
userProblem: A small project needs evidence of truthful spatial value, not an open-ended benchmark effort.
proposal: Run the staged proof on eight directed short clips and actual narrated product recordings, with raw-video and change-keyframe baselines. Require truth/provenance, useful spatial coverage, personal task value and bounded resources. Allow one targeted method revision; reject or narrow stitching if it cannot pass. Do not turn unrun experiments into feasibility claims.
